claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 16 and I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit, but it depends on his circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or undertaking an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college at the moment. He finished his GCSEs and decided not to continue with his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 16, not in approved education or training, I need to ask a couple more questions to determine eligibility.

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, started an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. He's not working that much - he just helps out occasionally but nothing like 24 hours a week. He hasn't started an apprenticeship and he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?** If he has, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't done that. He's just been at home since finishing school, hasn't signed up with careers services or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also confirm a few basic details:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK, and are you responsible for him** (for example, providing for his food, clothes, and other needs)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. We live together here in the UK - in Manchester actually. And yes, I'm responsible for him - I provide everything he needs, food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **I'm sorry to inform you that you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

Here's why: While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, for children aged 16 or over, the rules require that they must be:
- In approved education or training (and under 20), OR
- Registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education)

Since Alex is 16, has finished his GCSEs, is not in approved education or training, and has not registered with careers services or the armed services, the eligibility criteria are not met.

**However**, if Alex's circumstances change - for example, if he:
- Returns to education or training
- Registers with a careers service
- Or joins the armed services

You may become eligible again. If any of these situations occur, you should contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility at that time.

I hope this clarifies your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and has finished his GCSEs. According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you can still qualify if the child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Alex is not in approved education or training. Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Alex has not registered with either of these services. Since Alex is 16, not in approved education or training, has not registered with careers services or the armed services, and is not working 24 hours or more per week or receiving benefits in his own right, the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit are not met. While you live with Alex in the UK and are responsible for him, these circumstances alone do not satisfy the requirement that a child aged 16 or over must be in approved education/training or registered with qualifying services.
